claims.claim: The 2013 study describes enzyme-independent ureidoglycine decay to glyoxylate, ammonia and urea. This is opposite the selected synthesis direction; protonation is represented separately by the balanced catalog equation.
claims.access_scope: Search-index text excerpt; direct page fetch blocked by CAPTCHA. Full paper and underlying decay experiments not reviewed.

claims.claim: The 2010 primary-study abstract reports NMR identification of S-ureidoglycine as the allantoate-amidohydrolase product, spontaneous ammonia release in vitro, and an enzyme yielding S-ureidoglycolate. That enzymatic conversion is not the three-product spontaneous breakdown reaction.
claims.access_scope: Publisher abstract; full text and supporting information not reviewed.

decision: Exclude this condensation only in a separately named sensitivity run, alongside the earlier allantoate-condensation exclusion. Do not promote a ureidoglycine aminohydrolase protein to this different equation.
blocking_reasons: No retrieved reference sequence in the pinned prior exact-reaction searches.
Reverse synthesis, stereoselectivity, physiological rate and Cannabis activity remain unestablished.
Spontaneous forward decomposition does not prove thermodynamic irreversibility or eliminate possible enzyme-catalyzed reverse chemistry.
next_test: Measure formation of stereochemically resolved ureidoglycine from glyoxylate, ammonium and urea under defined plant-relevant conditions, with no-enzyme controls and time courses; compare candidate-protein conditions only after identity and baseline chemistry are established.
